additions.reason: This is the central concept of the entire Torah and its dominant node. The Rebbe explicitly uses 'בִּבְחִינַת: וְהַחַיּוֹת רָצוֹא וָשׁוֹב' twice — once to characterize the betrothal moment, and once as the full verse including 'כְּמַרְאֵה הַבָּזָק'. Ratzoh-vashov is the named bechina to which all other concepts in this Torah are equated. It is the essential nature: transient revelation that is immediately concealed. From Ezekiel 1:14.
additions.source_quote: הוּא בִּבְחִינַת: וְהַחַיּוֹת רָצוֹא וָשׁוֹב (יחזקאל א)

additions.reason: The revealed connection of souls at the moment of betrothal is explicitly called a bechina of ratzoh-vashov. It is not a cause of ratzoh-vashov — the betrothal does not produce the advance-and-retreat; rather, the betrothal IS the advance-and-retreat pattern expressing itself in human life. The momentary nature (revealed immediately, then concealed because she is forbidden until the chuppah) makes it structurally identical to the living creatures' advance-and-retreat in the vision.
additions.source_quote: הוּא בִּבְחִינַת: וְהַחַיּוֹת רָצוֹא וָשׁוֹב כַּנַּ״ל

additions.reason: The oscillation between concealment (הֶעְלֵם) and revelation (גִּלּוּי) is the structural essence of ratzoh-vashov in this Torah. The text uses 'בְּהֶעְלֵם' three times and 'נִתְגַּלֶּה' to describe the same dynamic. While not labeled with an explicit stand-alone 'בִּבְחִינַת' marker of its own, it is the definitional content of what ratzoh-vashov means in this context, and the Rebbe's explanation of 'רָצוֹא וָשׁוֹב' ('because afterwards they separate') makes concealment-and-revelation the meaning of the term. This concept belongs in the same package as ratzoh-vashov as it is its direct unpacking.
additions.source_quote: כִּי אֵין יוֹדְעִין מֵהִתְאַחֲדוּת שֶׁלָּהֶם עַד הַשִּׁדּוּךְ... נִמְצָא שֶׁבִּשְׁעַת הַשִּׁדּוּךְ נִתְגַּלֶּה אוֹר הָאַחְדוּת שֶׁלָּהֶם שֶׁהָיָה עַד עַתָּה בְּהֶעְלֵם, וְתֵכֶף וּמִיָּד נִתְעַלֵּם

additions.reason: The breaking of the clay vessel at betrothal is presented as hinting at (מְרַמֵּז) the secret of ratzoh-vashov. The Rebbe's explanation is that the verse 'רָצוֹא וָשׁוֹב כְּמַרְאֵה הַבָּזָק' means 'like the light that comes from the clay shards' — i.e., the Rebbe identifies the biblical 'בָּזָק' with the spark from broken clay. Therefore breaking the clay vessel IS (not causes, but IS) the manifestation of the ratzoh-vashov principle — the spark is the advance (רָצוֹא) and its immediate extinguishing is the retreat (שׁוֹב). These are two expressions of the same transience.
additions.source_quote: זֶה מְרַמֵּז עַל סוֹד: וְהַחַיּוֹת רָצוֹא וָשׁוֹב כְּמַרְאֵה הַבָּזָק כַּנַּ״ל

additions.reason: The spark/flash that comes from the clay shards is explicitly explained as the meaning of 'כְּמַרְאֵה הַבָּזָק' in Ezekiel — 'כָּאוֹר הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַחֲרָסִין'. The Rebbe unpacks the biblical simile by identifying the 'lightning-flash' with the spark from broken pottery. This spark is itself a bechina of ratzoh-vashov because 'it lasts only for a moment' (שֶׁהוּא רַק לְפִי שָׁעָה). The spark, the flash, and the breaking-vessel are three facets of the same phenomenon: momentary blinding illumination followed by darkness.
additions.source_quote: כָּאוֹר הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַחֲרָסִין; דְּהַיְנוּ הַנִּיצוֹץ שֶׁיּוֹצֵא בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁשּׁוֹבְרִין כְּלִי חֶרֶס, שֶׁהוּא רַק לְפִי שָׁעָה

additions.reason: The souls of the couple are described as being 'one above' (אֶחָד לְמַעְלָה) — their unity is the divine/supernal reality whose partial revelation at betrothal creates the ratzoh-vashov dynamic. While not labeled with explicit 'בִּבְחִינַת' language, the souls of the couple are the subject whose concealed-unity is the very content of what gets revealed at betrothal. Their supernal oneness is the 'light of unity' (אוֹר הָאַחְדוּת) referenced in the text. This concept belongs in the same package as it is the source-reality of which ratzoh-vashov is the expression. Polarity is good because souls (נְשָׁמוֹת) belong to the domain of holiness.
additions.source_quote: כִּי (כָּל) אֵלּוּ נְשָׁמוֹת שֶׁל הַזִּוּוּג הֵם לְמַעְלָה אֶחָד

analysis_notes.good_evil_mirror: This Torah has no good/evil mirror structure. The teaching is about a neutral structural phenomenon — the ratzoh-vashov oscillation between concealment and revelation — expressed in a lifecycle event (betrothal). There is no opposing evil domain discussed. The 'souls above are one' carries a good/holy valence, but the Rebbe does not construct an evil mirror for this teaching.
analysis_notes.cross_references_in_text: The Rebbe himself points to two cross-references at the end: (1) Torah #60 (LM1) for another reason for breaking the vessel, and (2) Likutay Tinyana (LM2) at its end. These are eitza/thematic cross-references, not bechina relationships.
analysis_notes.torah_summary: Torah #265 is an extremely compact teaching (4 sentences). Its entire argument: the souls of a couple are one above; their unity is hidden until betrothal; at betrothal it is revealed and immediately concealed (they separate again until the chuppah); this is exactly the ratzoh-vashov pattern. The breaking of the clay vessel enacts this pattern physically — the spark from the clay shard IS the בָּזָק (lightning-flash) of Ezekiel 1:14 — a flash that lasts only a moment and then is gone. The teaching turns an Ezekielian vision into an explanation of a wedding custom. The dominant node is רָצוֹא וָשׁוֹב with degree 3 (connected to: betrothal-revelation, spark/flash, and concealment-revelation pattern).
